text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT - Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts on /v1/generate. Paging @oncall-ryan and SREs. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/kv-prefix-cache

alice: noticing a sharp spike in 5xx starting ~12:02 UTC (root thread). Gateway 504s and internal 5xx. Dashboards show request success dropping from 99.95% -> 96.2% across eu-west-1.

mike: I'm looking. Quick dump: prefix_cache.evictions per min jumped from ~50 -> 4800 at 12:01. Eviction hot shards showing constant thrashing. Possible eviction storm causing backend stalls and timeouts.

sophia: any recent deploys or config changes?

alice: no code deploys in last 6h. There was a config flip to reduce prefix cache TTL (ops-config: cache.prefix.ttl from 24h -> 1h) rolled out 3h ago, flagged in changelog: commit 9f3a7b2.

mike: that TTL reduction could cause mass repopulation, but the pattern looks like corruption on some prefix keys. Logs show repeated errors: `kv: invalid prefix entry` followed by `panic: handlePrefetch: nil pointer` on some workers. Example log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T12:01:03Z cache-worker-12 ERROR kv.go:452 "invalid prefix entry" prefix_id=0x7f8a3 err="checksum mismatch"
2026-03-14T12:01:03Z cache-worker-12 PANIC runtime.go:234 "nil pointer" goroutine=128
```

eng-sre: this looks like corruption in the prefix index + an eviction storm. Two simultaneous risks: (1) corrupted entries causing panics -> 5xx, (2) eviction storm causing thundering herd to origin store -> timeouts. Recommend immediate mitigation: 1) flip feature flag to disable prefix caching (`cache.prefix.enabled=false`) so requests fall back to KV origin; 2) roll cache-workers to clear in-memory corrupt state; 3) place temporary rate-limit on repopulation (refill throttle).

sophia: we should also notify support and mark impacted customers. @support-lisa can you prepare outreach?

support-lisa: starting triage. Preliminary affected customers: org-acme (high traffic), org-echo (some failing requests), a handful of dev trial accounts. I'll open status page draft.

oncall-ryan: I'm taking ownership. Executing mitigation step 1 now: flipping flag in production via config-service.

mike: posting commands I used for previous incidents (for runbook parity):
```bash
# flip feature flag (config service)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  https://config.redwood/api/flags/cache.prefix.enabled -d '{"value":false}'
# restart cache workers safely
kubectl rollout restart deploy/cache-worker --namespace=prod --selector=role=prefix
```

oncall-ryan: flag flip submitted at 12:07:18 UTC (transaction id tx-20260314-01). Config-service reported success.

incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: `cache.prefix.enabled` => false (by oncall-ryan). Automatic rollback disabled. Notifying autoscalers.

mike: rolling cache-worker pods now. Doing a staggered restart to avoid complete drop. 3 pods at a time.

alice: after flag flip saw initial error rate drop: 5xx from 3.4% -> 1.1% in 3 minutes. Gateway timeouts reduced but still above baseline. Some backend tasks still retrying due to in-flight panics.

sophia: what about customer-facing fallbacks? Are we serving degraded performance or changed fidelity?

support-lisa: customers on Dedicated might see increased latency. Hosted API users see some transient 5xx but we've started a status page: https://status.redwood/incident/1769954321 (draft). I'll post a templated message.

eng-sre: while restarts are in progress, we should also disable aggressive repopulation by setting `cache.repopulate.throttle=0.1` (10% of repop traffic) to avoid origin overload. Mike, can you push that?

mike: done. throttle set at 0.1 at 12:15 UTC. Monitoring origin RPS.

alice: origin RPS dropped from the spike and latencies recovered from 1.8s p95 -> 420ms p95 after throttle. 5xx trending down to 0.5% now.

sophia: good. Any sign of durable corruption in persistent cache files? We need to check on-disk kv store for checksum mismatches and possibly run a repair job.

mike: yes, `kv-checker` reports ~0.04% keys with checksum mismatch, mostly in shard 4 and 7. Plan: snapshot corrupt ranges, evict them from persistent store, and rebuild via controlled backfill. I'll coordinate with storage team.

eng-sre: agree. For now mitigation actions: (A) flag disabled, (B) worker restarts complete, (C) repop throttle applied, (D) backfill queued as low-priority. Also create a canary to re-enable prefix cache only after checks.

oncall-ryan: handoff note for next shift (tagging @alice and @mike): monitor 5xx and origin latency for next 4 hours; don't re-enable prefix cache without explicit approval and checksum fixes.

support-lisa: status page updated and send proactive emails to top impacted orgs. Copy of message: "We identified elevated error rates affecting some requests to /v1/generate. Our team has disabled prefix caching and applied throttles to stabilize traffic. We're working on a repair and will update. Severity: high; ETA for next update: 60 minutes."

alice: small follow-up: root cause hypothesis - the TTL reduction triggered mass repopulation which, combined with a latent bug in prefix index compaction code path, led to corrupted entries and eviction loops. The corrupted entries caused some workers to panic and get restarted, amplifying the repopulation and causing a feedback loop (eviction storm).

mike: going to open an internal issue with reproducer steps and attach kv-checker output. Assign to eng-runtime and storage teams.

eng-sre: post-incident actions (agreed): 1) revert TTL change until we validate compaction; 2) add strong checksums and guardrails to prevent corrupted prefix entries causing panics; 3) improve metrics to alert earlier on eviction rate anomalies; 4) add automatic soft-throttles when repopulation rate crosses threshold.

oncall-ryan: leaving the incident in stable mitigation state. 5xx now ~0.2% and trending to baseline. Handing to oncall evening shift: @alice will be primary.

alice: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep watch and coordinate the repair window. Thanks all. Ending incident channel once backfill plan is scheduled.

support-lisa: I'll send final customer note after we confirm no residual errors for 30 minutes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation complete -> prefix cache disabled, workers rolled, repop throttle applied. Severity downgraded to degraded. Postmortem owner: @mike. ETA for postmortem: 72h.

mike: creating postmortem doc and linking to runbook edits. We'll include remediation timeline, code patch for compaction guards, and a safe re-enable checklist.

sophia: thanks everyone. Lessons to capture: be cautious with TTL mass reduces; ensure compaction is fuzz-tested; add circuit-breaker on evictions.

alice: closing notes: no data loss, partial customer disruption confined to high-throughput customers. Final metrics snapshot attached to postmortem. Will re-open if issues reappear.
